headline: A ten-day lull in the Iran conflict meets a hiking Fed, a 5% 10-year and $100 crude across a fully halted weekend window, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday - five hours after the final slot in this window. No slot in the published 24 hours contains a tradable tape. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. WTI settled $100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent $103.87, a third consecutive decline. The macro backdrop is genuinely two-sided. On the tightening side, the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, stating that inflation remains elevated; the 10-year rose about 5bp Friday to hover near 5% as traders added to October hike bets, with $100 crude feeding the inflation channel. On the easing side, the single new item this run is today's Day 204 conflict update, which records a tenth consecutive day without an Iranian ballistic or drone launch at a host state - the longest pause of the resumed war - alongside CENTCOM reporting Hormuz oil and LNG shipments at a six-month high with primary transit lanes clear of mines, and Saudi crude flows through the Strait recovering to roughly 2.8M bpd in early September from about 700K bpd in August. Because the venue is closed for the entire window, Tail sits at its structural floor throughout: there is no mechanism by which mean reversion can fail inside a halted market. Tail eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt and drifts back to 6 across Sunday afternoon, reflecting accumulating untested weekend headline exposure ahead of an unpriced reopen rather than any observed price structure. Stress tracks a similar shape, reaching a window high of 26 in the final slots. Confidence is solid rather than high: the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified, but it is static, and Friday's marks age through every subsequent hour with no tape able to refresh them.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 16-18 through Friday's dispersed triple-witching cash session, then fell through 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final eighteen slots. Stress peaked at 49 in the Friday afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive hours before edging back to 24 by the last slot. Dominant mode moved from mixed through a single trend-up print at the Friday close into normal for the last 21 hours. Confidence declined steadily from 86 to 74 as the live tape gave way to the weekend and Friday's marks aged. No hour in the lookback is unavailable.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, five hours after the final slot here. No published hour contains a tradable tape, and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside the window - the next catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday. Tail holds 5 for two hours, eases to 4 through the deepest part of the halt from 20:00Z Saturday, returns to 5 from 05:00Z Sunday and reaches 6 from 12:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates toward an unpriced reopen. Stress mirrors that shape between 22 and a window high of 26, crossing into the moderate band in the final three slots. Confidence declines gently from 74 to 67 as Friday's verified marks age. Every step is a function of venue distance and accumulating unpriced information, not of observed price structure; dominant mode stays normal throughout because a halted venue has no structure to classify. Tail is capped at 6 rather than drifting higher because the strongest weekend evidence - a tenth day without an Iranian launch, Hormuz flows at a six-month high and a third consecutive crude decline - points toward de-escalation into the reopen.
